corrections.text: The article attributes the 'legally significant' threshold definition (contributing more than around 15 lines of copyright-significant code/text) to the GNU Project's maintainer guidelines at gnu.org/prep/maintain/maintain.html. That page could not be fetched at review time — both the automated snapshot fetch and an independent manual re-check timed out repeatedly on www.gnu.org specifically, while gcc.gnu.org (a different server) remained reachable throughout. The claim is consistent with how GCC's own verified AI policy page (gcc.gnu.org/ai-policy.html) uses and links to that exact definition, but it was not independently confirmed against the gnu.org page itself during this review.
